places.name: working tree
places.says: What is checked out. git replaces it whole; a definition above can name the files in it.

facts.name: origin does not answer
facts.says: the remote cannot be reached, or does not have what is asked for

facts.name: the branch cannot be fast-forwarded
facts.says: the other branch's history does not contain the branch's last commit

facts.name: the tag cannot be created
facts.says: git tag exits non-zero for a reason other than the name being taken

facts.name: origin rejects the push
facts.says: a ref is not a fast-forward of origin's, or origin refuses it for a reason of its own

facts.name: the switch fails
facts.says: git switch exits non-zero for a reason other than local changes

facts.name: a merge refuses a tree with changes it would overwrite
facts.says: git merge --ff-only stops when the working tree has uncommitted changes to files the merge changes. The part of the manual read does not say.

facts.name: origin's tag names the commit pushed
facts.says: origin already has the tag, on the commit the push sends
facts.only: origin's tags already has the member

fetch tags.says: git fetch origin --tags. An update to a tag that exists locally is rejected without --force; git 2.54 then exits 1, and still creates the other tags.

handles.says: The update is rejected, the other tags are created, and git exits 1.

handles.when: tags is given a key twice
handles.because: A remote holds one tag of each name.

handles.when: remote-tracking branch holds what is kept nowhere
handles.because: A remote-tracking branch is a copy of origin's branch, and a fetch makes it again.

commit.says: git commit: the working tree's changes become a new commit on the branch.

reset to the commit before.says: git reset --hard HEAD~1. The manual: overwrite all files and directories with the version from the commit.

handles.because: reset moves the branch as asked. It does not look for other holders of the commit.

handles.when: working tree holds what is kept nowhere
handles.because: --hard overwrites all files with the version from the commit.

switch.says: git switch <branch>. The manual: the operation is aborted if it leads to loss of local changes.

handles.when: working tree holds what is kept nowhere

fast-forward.says: git merge --ff-only <other>. The manual: when not possible, refuse to merge and exit with a non-zero status.

all: working tree holds what is kept nowhere
a merge refuses a tree with changes it would overwrite

tag.says: git tag <name>. The manual: -f replaces an existing tag instead of failing.

push the branch and the tag.do: push the branch and the tag
push the branch and the tag.says: git push --atomic origin <branch> <tag>: both refs are taken, or neither.

handles.when: origin's tag names the commit pushed
handles.because: the ref is already what the push sends, so git takes the push

handles.when: origin's tags already has the member
handles.says: An update to a tag origin already has on another commit is rejected without --force.

runs: push the branch and the tag
